text: Branch & Worktree 是一款面向 DSH Web 的分支与 worktree 插件。在新建会话区域，它加入分支选择控件，可选已有分支或输入新分支，并能自动生成分支名、预览路径。启用 worktree 后会创建独立检出并注册为 DSH 工作区；也可关闭开关，在干净的当前检出中切换分支。运行中的会话还可通过底部状态栏移入新 worktree。适合需要并行处理代码、希望每个会话使用独立 Git 工作目录的开发者；需要本机 Git。

Branch & Worktree adds branch controls to DSH Web. Choose or create a Git branch, preview an automatic name, and start a session in a registered worktree. It also supports in-place switching and moving a running session into a worktree. Requires Git.
想让每个 DSH 编码会话都在独立的 Git worktree 中运行。
新建 DSH 会话时，能不能先选分支或创建新分支？
我想并行处理几个代码任务，又不想反复 stash 当前改动。
帮我在 DSH 新会话页面加一个 Git 分支选择入口。
希望自动生成分支名，并在创建前看到 worktree 路径。
正在运行的 DSH 会话能否切换到新 worktree 继续工作？
I want each coding session to start in its own Git worktree.
Can I choose or create a branch from the DSH new session screen?
Branch & Worktree 的分支选择功能：在 DSH 新建会话行打开分支菜单，选择已有分支或输入新名称，并可指定基础分支。点击“从这里开始”后使用所选分支启动会话。
Branch & Worktree 的自动 worktree 功能：新建会话时默认生成并预览随机分支名及目录；确认后创建 Git worktree、注册工作区，并从该目录开始会话。
Branch & Worktree 的原地切换功能：关闭创建 worktree 开关后，可在当前检出中切换到选择的已有分支；工作区存在未提交改动时会拒绝切换。
Branch & Worktree 的运行中会话迁移功能：会话底部状态栏提供新建 worktree 入口，创建后把同一会话的工作目录切到新路径。
Branch & Worktree 使用本机 Git 在所选仓库内创建 .worktrees 目录及分支；卸载插件不会自动移除已创建的 worktree 或分支。

dsh-branch-worktree README · dsh-branch-worktree：English | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) Web UI plugin that adds a **branch picker with automatic Git worktree creation** to the New Session screen.

Pick the branch (or type a new branch name) right next to the workspace and agent-mode chips, then let DSH create an isolated checkout for it. The conversation starts inside that checkout, so nothing you have half-edited in your main working copy gets disturbed.

dsh-branch-worktree README · Why：The New Session screen lets you choose a **workspace** and an **agent mode**, but a conversation always starts in the workspace directory as it is, on whichever branch is currently checked out. Parallel agent work therefore means juggling branches, stashing changes, or creating worktrees by hand before every session.

This plugin closes that gap with one extra chip:

dsh-branch-worktree README · Why：| Control | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| Workspace / project | DSH built-in |
| Agent mode (e.g. Creator) | DSH built-in |
| **Branch, or new branch + base** | **this plugin** |
| **Automatic worktree** | **this plugin** |

dsh-branch-worktree README · What it does：- **Sits between the workspace and agent-mode chips** — the row reads project → branch → mode, which is exactly the order in which those decisions are made.
- **Opens as a dropdown, not a modal** — the composer stays visible and usable behind it.
- **Names itself by default** — with the worktree switch already on, the panel opens ready to go: the plugin generates both the branch name and the worktree directory name, previews them, and creates exactly what it previewed. Start a session without typing a branch name at all.
- **Pick an existing branch, or type a new name** — turn automatic naming off to choose the branch yourself. A new branch is created from the base you choose (defaults to the repository's own default); an existing branch is reused instead of being recreated.
- **Toggles between two modes:**
  - **Create a worktree** (default) — `git worktree add` under `<repo>/.worktrees/<branch>`, then registers that directory as a DSH Workspace and starts the session there. Your current checkout is never touched, so uncommitted work stays exactly where it was.
  - **Switch in place** — `git checkout` the branch in the current checkout. Re

dsh-branch-worktree README · Install：Requires DSH `>= 0.2.0` and `git` on `PATH`.

dsh-branch-worktree README · From the Web UI (recommended)：1. Open the sidebar → **Plugins** → **Add plugin** → **Install a third-party plugin** (accepts npm packages, Git repositories, and local directories).
2. Paste the Git repository address:

```
   https://github.com/elfgzp/dsh-branch-worktree
   ```

3. Confirm, then switch on **Branch & Worktree** under **Installed plugins**. Restart DSH if the UI does not pick it up right away.

dsh-branch-worktree README · Ask your agent to install it：In a DSH session with the plugin-manager tool enabled (Creator mode has it), just say:

> 从 https://github.com/elfgzp/dsh-branch-worktree 安装这个插件并启用

or in English:

> Install the plugin at https://github.com/elfgzp/dsh-branch-worktree and enable it

The agent calls `plugin_manager` with `install_bundle`, which adds the dependency to your profile, appends the bundle to `dsh.profile.bundles`, and activates it.

text:
dsh-branch-worktree README · Manual, for development：```bash
git clone https://github.com/elfgzp/dsh-branch-worktree
cd dsh-branch-worktree
```

Then install that absolute directory through **Plugins → Add plugin → Install a third-party plugin**. The profile records it as a `link:` dependency, so later edits need only a restart (or a page reload for the browser half).

> Never hand-edit the profile's `package.json` or `cordis.patch.yml`. The plugin manager owns those files; editing them directly desynchronizes the bundle list.

dsh-branch-worktree README · Usage：1. Click **New Session**.
2. Choose your workspace, then click the **branch chip** in the middle.
3. Press **Start here** straight away — automatic naming and the worktree switch are both on by default, so the branch and worktree names are generated for you.
4. To name things yourself, turn **Auto name** off, then pick an existing branch or type a name under *New branch* — a *based on* picker then appears.
5. Press **Start here** (or hit Enter in the name field).
dsh-branch-worktree README · Usage：The session opens in the resulting directory, and the workspace appears in the sidebar under the branch name.

dsh-branch-worktree README · Automatic naming：- Generated branches live under a `wt/` namespace, so they are easy to tell apart from branches you named yourself.
- The name is **random and readable**: an adjective, a noun, and a short tag — `wt/brave-otter-7f3a`.
- **It is never derived from your conversation.** A worktree name is a durable Git ref that outlives the prompt that happened to be in the box: deriving it from a draft would leak prompt text into branch names, into `git log` output, and into anything the branch is pushed to — and two unrelated branches would collide on the same sentence. The draft still travels with you into the new session; it just does not name the branch.
- Collisions are retried automatically against **both** existing branches and `.worktrees/` directory names, including the ones that only collide after the slash is flattened (`wt/a-b` and `wt/a/b` both map to `wt-a-b`).
- The panel **previews the name and path** under *Will create* before you commit, so automatic never means opaque.
- What is previewed is what is created: the displayed name is sent to the Host verbatim.
dsh-branch-worktree README · Automatic naming：Turn **Auto name** off to get exactly the manual behavior described below.

dsh-branch-worktree README · Moving a running session into a new worktree：The New Session chip only exists while the session is blank. Once a conversation
is running there is a second entry point: a thin **status bar across the bottom
of the window** shows the current working directory, and — while that directory
is a Git repository that is not already a worktree — a **New worktree** button.
section: Moving a running session into a new worktree

text:
dsh-branch-worktree README · Moving a running session into a new worktree：Clicking it creates a `wt/…` worktree and moves **that same session** onto it.
No second workspace appears in the sidebar and no second conversation is
opened: the Host appends a durable working-directory change to the running
conversation, which is the same mechanism the shipped `create_worktree` tool
uses. The model is notified by the Host, so you never have to type "I moved the
files, go look there" yourself.
section: Moving a running session into a new worktree

dsh-branch-worktree README · Moving a running session into a new worktree：The bar hides itself as soon as the directory is inside `.worktrees/`, so it
stops offering a switch once you are already isolated.

text: dsh-branch-worktree README · What the worktree toggle actually does：This is the part that is easy to misread: **"Create worktree" does not imply "create branch"**. The rule is:
section: What the worktree toggle actually does

text:
dsh-branch-worktree README · What the worktree toggle actually does：| The branch name you give | What runs |
|---|---|
| **Automatic** (default) | Generates an unused `wt/…` branch and runs `git worktree add -b` — **creates the branch** in a new worktree |
| **Does not exist** | `git worktree add -b <branch> <path> <base>` — **creates the branch** and checks it out in the new worktree |
| **Already exists** | `git worktree add <path> <branch>` — **reuses the branch**, creating nothing |
| **Checked out in another worktree** | Refused, because Git will not check out the same branch twice |
| **Checked out in the main working copy** | Refused, instead of handing the main checkout back as if it were a worktree |
section: What the worktree toggle actually does

text:
dsh-branch-worktree README · What the worktree toggle actually does：That last row matters: previously, selecting the current branch with the worktree switch on returned the main checkout itself (`reusedWorktree: true`) — the switch appeared to work while isolating nothing. That combination is now an explicit error, so the switch means what it says.

So a new name starts a new branch, an existing name reuses one, and you never get a surprise duplicate or a silently skipped worktree. The dropdown says which path is about to be taken before you commit to it.

Nothing is ever deleted by this plugin. To retire a worktree:

```bash
git worktree remove .worktrees/feature-login
git branch -d feature/login
```

dsh-branch-worktree README · Errors you may see：| Message | Meaning |
|---|---|
| This workspace is not inside a Git repository. | The selected workspace has no `.git`; the chip would not have been shown if this was known up front. |
| Branch names accept letters, digits and `. _ / -` only. | The typed branch name is not a valid Git ref. |
| That branch is already checked out in another worktree. | Git will not check out the same branch twice. Pick another branch, or create a new one. |
| That branch is checked out in your main working copy. | The main checkout is not a worktree, so it cannot be isolated. Pick another branch, or turn automatic naming on. |
| A worktree directory with that name already exists. | A stale directory is in the way at `.worktrees/<branch>`. Remove it with `git worktree prune` or by hand. |
| Your current checkout has uncommitted changes. | You turned the worktree option off while the tree was dirty. Turn it back on, or commit/stash first. |
| Git refused the operation. | Any other Git failure; the Git message is shown in the dialog. |

dsh-branch-worktree README · How it works：```
┌──────────────────────── Browser (client.js) ────────────────────────┐
│  conversation.hero.options slot occupant                            │
│    button  ──► Modal: branch select / new branch / worktree switch  │
│                        │                                            │

Two details are worth knowing:

dsh-branch-worktree README · How it works：- **The session must be *created* in the worktree, not moved into it.** A DSH session's `header.cwd` is frozen creation metadata: the system prompt's cwd, the shell tool's default workdir, and the sandbox's `workspaceRoot` all derive from it. The plugin therefore registers the worktree as a Workspace and opens a blank session there, rather than mutating an existing session.
- **All Git work runs on the Host, never in the browser**, and always through `execFile` with a literal argv — no shell interpolation of branch names. Every route validates against the connection trust fence first, so a page from another origin cannot drive Git on your machine.

dsh-branch-worktree README · Where it registers：| Half | Surface |
|---|---|
| Host | `webServer` exact routes `/branch-worktree/inspect`, `/branch-worktree/suggest`, `/branch-worktree/create` |
| Client | `conversation.hero.options` (list slot), id `branch-worktree`, order `-10` |

dsh-branch-worktree README · Where it registers：On sitting *between* the workspace and agent-mode chips: DSH ships **no slot** in that position. `conversation.hero.workspace` and `conversation.hero.agentPreset` are `display: contents` wrappers, and the only slot meant for extra controls — `conversation.hero.options` — is right-aligned at the end of the row. The plugin therefore injects a small scoped stylesheet that makes that container `display: contents` and uses `order` to place itself between the two shipped chips. The selectors are `:has()`-scoped to the New Session row, so conversation views are untouched, no other plugin's nodes are moved, and the block becomes irrelevant the day DSH grows a real slot there.

dsh-branch-worktree README · Where it registers：It depends on the shipped `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-conversation` plugin only, and uses no private APIs beyond the documented `webServer`, `connection`, `workspaceRegistry`, `slots`, `locale`, and `uiWorkspace` services.

dsh-branch-worktree README · Compatibility：| DSH | Status |
|---|---|
| `0.2.1-rc.3` | tested |
| `>= 0.2.0` | expected to work |

Both `en` and `zh` locales ship with the plugin; the UI follows the DSH language setting.

dsh-branch-worktree README · Uninstall：**Plugins** → **Branch & Worktree** → **Remove**. Worktrees and branches this plugin created are left on disk; clean them up with the `git worktree remove` commands shown above.
dsh-branch-worktree README · Prior art：Before writing this, I looked for an existing plugin that covered the whole flow. These are the ones that exist:

dsh-branch-worktree README · Prior art：| Repository | Stars | Why it was not enough |
|---|---|---|
| [frederico-kluser/dsh-worktree-jump](https://github.com/frederico-kluser/dsh-worktree-jump) | 2 | Worktree jumping only; no branch picker at session creation |
| [Letter2025/dsh-task-worktree](https://github.com/Letter2025/dsh-task-worktree) | 2 | Task isolation, no project/mode-integrated control |
| [YS-BW/dsh-plugins](https://github.com/YS-BW/dsh-plugins) | 1 | General plugin collection |
| [zhang-guo-wen/dsh-worktree](https://github.com/zhang-guo-wen/dsh-worktree) | 0 | Incomplete |
| [epik7th/dsh-task-worktree](https://github.com/epik7th/dsh-task-worktree) | 0 | Incomplete |
| [d0nj/dsh-plugins](https://github.com/d0nj/dsh-plugins) | 0 | General plugin collection |

dsh-branch-worktree README · Prior art：None combined *project + agent mode + branch + automatic worktree* in the New Session row, so this plugin does exactly that and nothing else.

Note that DSH already ships a non-GUI worktree capability — `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-worktree` with its `create_worktree` model tool — but it is off by default in every shipped profile and is model-driven rather than part of the New Session flow. This plugin complements it; the two do not conflict.
